 El Nino maintains its very strong intensity, with heavy rains concentrated in central Vietnam.
 According to the National Center for Meteorological and Hydrological Forecasting, from December 2026 to February 2027, the El Nino phenomenon will continue to maintain a very strong intensity with a high probability of 79%.
 Báo Tin Tức • 16/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Roads in Hoa Chau ward ( Hue ) are deeply flooded, making travel difficult. Photo: Van Dung/TTXVN Heavy rains are occurring in Central Vietnam. 
 Regarding weather patterns from December 2026 to February 2027, the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting reports that in December, the Central region may still experience moderate to heavy rainfall, concentrated in the area from Ha Tinh to Hue city and the South Central Coast. However, it is important to note the possibility of a deficit in total rainfall compared to the multi-year average in many areas of the Central region even during the rainy season. Moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to decrease in January 2027.
 Regarding total rainfall in the months, in Northern Vietnam, December had a total rainfall 5-15mm higher than the multi-year average, while the area from Thanh Hoa to northern Quang Tri generally had rainfall close to the multi-year average. From southern Quang Tri to Hue city, rainfall was generally 20-40mm lower than the multi-year average. The South Central Coastal region had 50-150mm lower than the multi-year average. The Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam had a total rainfall 10-20mm lower than the multi-year average for the same period.
 In January 2027, rainfall in Northern Vietnam and the area from Thanh Hoa to Ha Tinh will generally be close to the multi-year average; other areas will experience 10-30mm less rainfall than the multi-year average; the Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam will experience little rain. In February, rainfall in Northern Vietnam is likely to be close to the multi-year average; Central Vietnam will experience 10-20mm less rainfall than the multi-year average; the Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam will experience little rain.
 In the Mekong River basin, total rainfall in the upper reaches in December is generally 10-20% higher than the multi-year average for the same period. January and February 2027 are generally low-rainfall. In the middle reaches from December 2026 to January 2027, rainfall is generally 10-30% lower than the multi-year average; however, in the northern part of the region, rainfall in December 2026 is approximately the same as the multi-year average for the same period. February is generally low-rainfall. In the lower reaches, rainfall in December 2026 is generally 20-40% lower than the multi-year average. In January 2027, rainfall is 30-60% lower than the multi-year average for the same period. February is generally low-rainfall.
 The average temperature trend across the country from December 2026 to February 2027 is expected to be 1-2 degrees Celsius higher than the multi-year average for the same period. In the Southeast region, hot weather is likely to appear from February 2027, earlier than the multi-year average.
 Cold air masses are likely to be weaker than the multi-year average. Severe cold spells are likely to occur later than usual; the number of days with severe cold spells in Northern Vietnam and North Central Vietnam will generally be lower than the multi-year average for the same period. However, there is still a possibility of short-lived periods of severe cold spells causing sharp temperature drops.
 "From December 2026 to February 2027, the number of storms and tropical depressions active in the East Sea region is likely to be lower than the multi-year average, with little chance of making landfall (the multi-year average in the East Sea is 1.4 storms; making landfall is 0.2 storms). Across the country, there is a possibility of dangerous weather phenomena such as thunderstorms, tornadoes, lightning, hail, and strong gusts of wind," noted Nguyen Duc Hoa, Deputy Head of the Climate Forecasting Department.
 You may also like From March to May 2027, hot weather is expected to intensify. 
 The National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting predicts that from March to May, the average temperature nationwide will generally be 1-2 degrees Celsius higher than the multi-year average for the same period, with some areas exceeding 2 degrees Celsius. From March, heatwaves are expected to intensify in the Central Highlands and Southern Vietnam. Localized heatwaves are possible in the Northwest and North Central regions starting in March. In April and May, heatwaves are expected to increase and expand across the Northern and Central regions.
 During this period, the El Niño phenomenon is likely to continue with a probability of about 80%, although its intensity tends to weaken significantly. A weak to moderate El Niño will predominate with a probability of about 78%, while a strong El Niño will only account for about 2%; the probability of transitioning to a neutral ENSO state is about 20%.
 Regarding the total rainfall during the forecast period, the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting reported that in March, rainfall in the North and Central regions was 10-20mm lower than the multi-year average, with generally little rain in the Central Highlands and Southern regions. In April, rainfall in the North is likely to be 10-20mm lower than the multi-year average; the Central and Southern regions tend to be 20-40mm lower than the multi-year average. In May, rainfall is generally 10-35% lower than the multi-year average for the same period, except for the mountainous areas of the Northeast where the total rainfall is generally close to the multi-year average for the same period.
 Specifically, rainfall in the Northern region in March is generally 20-50mm, with some areas receiving more. In April, it is generally 40-100mm, with some areas receiving more. In May, it is generally 140-190mm, with some areas receiving even more.
 In the Central region, rainfall in March is commonly 30-60mm. In April, it is commonly 40-70mm. In May, it is commonly 70-150mm.
 In the Central Highlands and Southern regions, March generally sees little rainfall (10-20mm/month). April typically receives 40-80mm, with some areas receiving even less. May generally receives 110-190mm, with some areas receiving even less. The rainy season in this region is likely to arrive later than the average for the same period in previous years.
 In March, the Mekong River basin experienced a 15-30% deficit in total rainfall in the upper and middle reaches compared to the multi-year average, and a 20-50% deficit in the lower reaches compared to the multi-year average. In April, the entire basin experienced a 20-50% deficit compared to the multi-year average. In May, the entire basin experienced a 15-30% deficit compared to the multi-year average.
 Deputy Head of the Climate Forecasting Department Nguyen Duc Hoa emphasized that from March to May, there is little chance of typhoons or tropical depressions appearing in the East Sea (the multi-year average in the East Sea is 0.8 storms; making landfall is 0 storms). Cold air masses tend to be weaker than the multi-year average. During the late winter period, the number of days with light rain or drizzle in the North is likely to be less than the multi-year average.
 You may also like Additionally, showers and thunderstorms are possible in the Northern and North Central regions, with localized moderate to heavy rainfall. From May onwards, thunderstorms will increase in the Central Highlands and Southern regions, and will continue to occur in the Northern and North Central regions. During thunderstorms, be wary of tornadoes, lightning, hail, and strong gusts of wind.
 Meteorological and hydrological experts warn that the Northeast monsoon may cause strong winds and large waves in the East Sea, affecting maritime activities and fishing. In addition, heavy rain, thunderstorms, tornadoes, lightning, hail, and severe cold weather could adversely affect production, public health, crops, and livestock. From around May, the Southwest monsoon is likely to become active and cause strong winds in the southern sea areas.
 Furthermore, during the period from March to May, the Central Highlands and Southern regions are likely to experience rainfall shortages, combined with high temperatures and the possibility of a late rainy season, increasing the risk of drought and water scarcity for daily life and production, affecting agricultural production and people's livelihoods.
 In the context of climate change, weather and climate patterns are becoming increasingly complex with many dangerous and extreme forms such as heatwaves, heavy rainfall in short periods, flash floods, landslides, etc. Therefore, meteorological and hydrological agencies propose regularly updating and integrating meteorological and hydrological forecast and warning information into short-term bulletins (1-3 days) to promptly adjust production plans and response measures, especially reservoir operation plans, ensuring the safety of structures and downstream areas, as well as ensuring the safety of production activities and people's lives.
